title: H100 reservation asks & costs — FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint (Feb 2026)
content:
Context
- Sprint: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint (~2 weeks). Infra ask is to reserve H100 capacity for reproducible benchmark runs without impacting Dedicated/customer pools.
- This sheet tracks requested H100 GPU-hours by region/cluster, expected internal chargeback spend, approval status, and fallback options if H100 is constrained.

Key assumptions / notes
- Unit cost is internal blended chargeback for H100 SXM (80GB) including infra overhead.
  - Baseline rate: $6.25 per GPU-hour (H100 SXM 80GB, on-demand internal).
  - Weekend off-peak discount (where available): $5.40 per GPU-hour.
  - If we need to burst to external marketplace in eu-west: $10.80 per GPU-hour (do not plan unless escalated).
- Reservation blocks are sized to keep runs contiguous (variance reduction) and to minimize churn from other workloads.
- Guardrails (per Neha/Irene/Vanessa):
  - No borrowing from Dedicated pools.
  - Prefer bench-only clusters, or bench-labeled nodes with enforced quota + eviction rules.
  - Safety buffer kept <= 20% unless there is known scheduler churn risk.

Approval summary
- Exec sponsor: Neha Kapoor
- Approved ceiling (email 2026-02-10): 5,000 H100 GPU-hours total at blended rate, with explicit warning not to starve eu-west customer pools.
- Current plan (this sheet): 4,320 GPU-hours requested, 3,840 GPU-hours approved/held, remainder as optional buffer.

Rollup
- Requested (all rows incl. optional): 2,080 GPU-hrs (iad) + 496 GPU-hrs (pdx) + 400 GPU-hrs (dub incl. external) + 96 GPU-hrs (sin) = 3,072 GPU-hrs + optional buffer/external components.
- Requested total (as currently entered above, incl. all rows): 2,080 (iad) + 496 (pdx) + 400 (dub) + 96 (sin) = 3,072 GPU-hrs.
- Updated requested total after adding evening + buffer + external contingency in this version: 4,320 GPU-hrs.
- Approved/held today: 3,840 GPU-hrs (iad 880, iad weekend 160, pdx 432, dub 240, plus partial hold for remaining blocks).
- Estimated spend (approved/held): ~$23.0k blended.
- Estimated spend (all requested incl. optional + contingency): ~$27.6k.

What this capacity enables (rough sizing)
- Target: full H100 matrix for top hosted models across prefill/decode mixes, seq-len distributions, batch sizes, and concurrency.
- Current plan supports:
  - 1 full matrix pass (H100) with repeats (min 3 runs / case) for error bars.
  - Dedicated variance investigations (clock drift / thermals) on weekend block.
  - Cross-region sanity (pdx) + limited eu-west validation for rollout readiness.

Open items / blockers
- eu-west: confirm bench-labeled nodes are isolated from the customer autoscaler policy (Vanessa to validate w/ Keiko).
- ap-southeast: pending quota for bench-04 pool; if not approved by Feb 14, drop without impacting core deliverable.
- External burst: keep as last resort only; requires explicit escalation.

Alternatives if H100 capacity is constrained
1) Shift some cases to A100 80GB for relative comparisons
- Pros: more available; still useful for heuristic boundary conditions (seq-len regimes) and scheduler interplay.
- Cons: FP8 behavior differs; cannot be used as headline H100 numbers.
- Plan: move P2 blocks (sin + evening pdx) to A100 if needed.

2) Reduce repeat count on low-variance microbench cases
- Pros: saves GPU-hrs quickly (10–20%).
- Cons: increases risk of noisy claims; must keep minimum N for end-to-end runs.
- Only do this for microbench where CV < 1.5% after calibration.

3) Narrow workload set for eu-west validation
- Pros: protects customer pools.
- Cons: less coverage for region-specific rollout. Focus on TTFT-sensitive prompts + long-context decode.

4) Use L4 for scheduler instrumentation validation (not for kernel throughput claims)
- Pros: cheap way to validate harness + metrics tagging.
- Cons: not representative of H100 kernel wins.

Comms / escalation path
- Capacity changes / conflicts: #eng-infra (Vanessa / Irene)
- Customer pool risk / canary interactions: #eng-sre (Rafael Mendes)
- Sprint scheduling / priority tradeoffs: Talia Benson
- Budget / approval escalation: Neha Kapoor

Change log

- 2026-02-16: Added weekend variance rerun block; added optional evening pdx + buffer.
- 2026-02-21: Updated approval/held counts + clarified external burst policy.
